paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Factorization (VQF) using Different Variations of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)

summary: The paper simulates Variational Quantum Factorization (VQF) using QAOA variants on Qiskit to factor integers 143, 291311, and 175 using 4, 6, and 3 qubits respectively. The best success probabilities reported are 0.92 for 143 (maQAOA), 0.56 for 291311 (CVaR‑maQAOA with α=0.75), and 0.99 for 175 (maQAOA). Results are obtained entirely via noiseless simulation with no classical baseline comparison.

experiments.description: Simulation study of variational quantum factorization (VQF) for factoring 143, 291311, and 175 using standard QAOA, multi-angle QAOA, CVaR QAOA, and CVaR multi-angle QAOA on Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA; multi-angle QAOA (maQAOA); CVaR QAOA; CVaR maQAOA
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA ansatz with alternating problem and mixer unitaries

hyperparameters.standard_qaoa_parameters: shared beta and gamma per layer
hyperparameters.maqaoa_parameters: distinct beta and gamma parameters per gate per layer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary factorization variables mapped to qubits; 1 qubit per binary variable in the reduced VQF formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the Ising-form objective derived from VQF. For 143, the reduced classical objective is \u0304f(x)=5-3p0-p1-q0+2p0q0-3p1q0+2p0p1q0-3q1+p0q1+2p1q1+2p1q0q1.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty-free reduction via algebraic simplification of multiplication clauses; CVaR uses top-α fraction of measurement outcomes in expectation estimation.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: For 143: Hc = -σz0σz1σz2/4 + σz0σz1/4 + 3σz0σz2/4 + σz0σz3/4 + σz0/2 - σz1σz2σz3/4 - σz1σz2/4 + 3σz1σz3/4 + σz1/4 + σz2σz3/4 + σz2/4 + σz3/2 + 2

problem_instance.description: Factorization of bi-prime numbers 143 and 291311, and tri-prime number 175.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Binary multiplication clauses were simplified using rules from Anschuetz et al. to reduce higher-order terms before mapping to an Ising Hamiltonian.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Success probability measured from quantum simulation measurement statistics; highest success probability reported across tested QAOA variants and layer counts.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: QAOA/CVaR objective evaluation and parameter optimization in simulation; factorization clauses reduced before Hamiltonian construction.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement bitstrings interpreted as factors; success counted when product of inferred factors equals target number.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: success probability vs number of layers p

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline or speedup analysis is reported; the paper only compares success probabilities across QAOA variants in simulation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; experiments only simulate 3–6 qubit circuits for small integer factorization instances.
limiting_factors: no comparison with classical factoring algorithms
no asymptotic complexity or scaling study

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly states Qiskit quantum simulation framework and does not name a real QPU.
num_qubits not given as a single global value; inferred per instance from the paper's stated qubit counts (4 for 143, 6 for 291311, 3 for 175).
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only QAOA layer count p is discussed, so depth is not available as a concrete value.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; the paper only compares empirical success probabilities across QAOA variants.
The paper compares QAOA variants only and does not benchmark against classical factoring algorithms.
All experiments are small-scale simulations; therefore no empirical quantum advantage claim is made.
